pr.title: Invoice search, share link, notes and CSV export
pr.author: Crashtest author agent

issue.title: Invoice search, share link, notes and CSV export
issue.body:
As someone who sends a lot of invoices, I want to find invoices quickly, share one with a client without making them sign up, keep a note on an invoice, and take my list into a spreadsheet, so I spend less time hunting through pages and answering "can you send that again?" emails.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On the invoice list I can search by client name or invoice number. Search combines with the status filter, and both survive paging.
2. Each row of the invoice list also shows how many line items the invoice has.
3. An invoice has a free-text notes field. I can edit it; it shows on the invoice page.
4. I can create a public share link for an invoice. Anyone with the link sees a read-only page of that invoice (client, line items, total, notes) without signing in. I can revoke the link, after which it shows "not found".
5. I can export the invoices I am looking at (current search and filter) as a CSV file.
6. Everything that worked before still works.

intro: This change adds four things to invoices: search on the list page, a free-text notes field, a public share link that can be revoked, and a CSV export of the current list. Each list row also shows how many line items the invoice has. Two new database columns hold the notes and the share token, and older databases get them when they are opened.

stops.why: Notes and share links both need a place on the invoice row. A database created before this change already has an `invoices` table, so the code adds the columns to it when the database is opened.

blocks.text: Two new fields on `Invoice` carry the notes and the share link. Look at their types: one is always a string, the other can be null.

notes.text: null means the invoice has no share link.

blocks.text: A new database gets the columns directly from the `CREATE TABLE` statement.
For an existing database `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does nothing, because the table is already there. **`applySchema` handles that case.** Read what it checks before each `ALTER TABLE`.

notes.text: A partial index: only rows that have a token are in it.
Runs after the loop, because the index needs the `share_token` column.
Before this change the line was `db.exec(SCHEMA)`.

Stops two invoices from having the same share token
Adds a column to an existing table only when it is missing

blocks.text: `resetSchema` drops all tables and builds them again. The seed script calls it. It now uses the same function.

questions.explain: Line 156 lists the columns of the table and line 157 runs `ALTER TABLE` only when the column name is not in that list.

stops.title: The search text is cleaned, then bound as a LIKE parameter
stops.why: The issue asks for search by client name or invoice number that combines with the status filter. One helper builds the search part of the WHERE clause and a second helper joins it with the status part, so every query can use the same filter.

blocks.text: Every route passes the raw `q` value from the URL through `parseSearch` first. The import list at the top was only reformatted, with one new type added.

notes.text: The `Invoice` type is used by the share-link lookup later in this file.
`MAX_NOTES` belongs to the notes feature, shown in a later stop.

blocks.text: `searchClause` turns the cleaned text into a piece of SQL and its parameters. **The user text never becomes part of the SQL string.** Look at what is done with `%` and `_` before the pattern is built. Then see how `filterClause` puts workspace, status and search together.

notes.text: An empty search adds nothing, so the query stays as it was before.
The same pattern is bound twice: once for the client name and once for the invoice number.

focus.why: Escapes % and _ and binds user text as a parameter
Keeps one workspace from reading another's invoices

questions.prompt: A user searches for `50%`. Which invoices can match?
options: Those whose client name or number contains the text `50%`
Those that contain `50` anywhere, because `%` matches any text
Those whose client name or number starts with `50`
None, because the query fails on the `%` sign
questions.explain: Line 55 puts a backslash before `%`, `_` and backslash, and line 56 declares the backslash as the ESCAPE character. So `%` in the user text matches only a real percent sign.

questions.prompt: The status is `overdue` and the search is `acme`. Which parameter list does `filterClause` return?
options: [workspaceId, 'overdue', '%acme%', '%acme%']
[workspaceId, '%acme%', '%acme%', now]
[workspaceId, now, '%acme%', '%acme%']
[workspaceId, 'sent', now, '%acme%', '%acme%']
questions.explain: Lines 63 to 65 write 'sent' into the SQL text and push only `now`. Line 71 then appends the two search patterns after the status parameters.

`listInvoices` runs two queries. The first counts invoices for the tabs, the second fetches one page of rows. Check which parts of the filter each query uses, and **where `total` comes from**.

notes.text: The join is added only when there is a search, because only the search clause reads `c.name`.
The order follows the `?` marks in the SQL: date, workspace, then the patterns.
Filter parameters come first, then page size and offset.

focus.why: Count query has its own workspace filter; parameter order must match
Sums the rounded line amounts into the invoice total in cents
Row query is limited to the workspace by this WHERE clause
Parameter order must match the ? marks, workspace id first

blocks.text: The JSON API uses the same function. It needs one more import.
The API list reads `q` in the same way as the page and returns the count with each invoice.

notes.text: The API calls the field `line_items`. The value is the same count.

focus.why: Workspace comes from the session, never from the request

questions.prompt: The Paid tab is open. The search matches 30 invoices and 12 of them are paid. What is `total` in the result?
options: The number of all paid invoices in the workspace
questions.explain: The count query on lines 82 to 92 is narrowed by the search, and line 100 takes `counts[status]`. For the Paid tab that is the number of paid matches.

The invoice is left out of the list

questions.prompt: The Paid tab is open with the search `acme`. Which number does the line under the heading show?

stops.title: The CSV export reuses the list filter and makes formula text harmless
stops.why: The issue asks for an export of the invoices the user is looking at. The route uses the same filter builder as the list, and the CSV writer treats client names, references and notes as untrusted text that a spreadsheet could run.

blocks.text: The Export CSV link on the list page leads here. The path is under `/invoices/*`, which `requirePage` already protects, so the route has a signed-in user. It parses `status` and `q` in the same way as the list page.

blocks.title: From the export link to the downloaded file

notes.text: The same `displayStatus` as the list, so a sent invoice past its due date is exported as overdue.
`attachment` tells the browser to save the file and not to show it.

focus.why: Export is limited to the signed-in user's workspace
Turns cents into euros in the export

notes.text: The same filter builder as `listInvoices`, so list and export agree on what matches.

focus.why: Builds the workspace, status and search filter for the export
Computes each exported total in cents from the line items

blocks.text: `toCsv` turns the rows into text and sends each value through `csvField`. **Client names, references and notes are user text, and a spreadsheet may run text as a formula.** See what the function does about that.

notes.text: Numbers skip both checks that follow. The line item count is passed as a number.
A field with a comma, a quote or a line break is wrapped in quotes, and quotes inside it are doubled.

questions.prompt: A client is named `=SUM(A1)`. How does this name appear in the CSV file?
options: `=SUM(A1)`, unchanged
`=SUM(A1)` wrapped in double quotes
As an empty field
`'=SUM(A1)`, with an apostrophe in front
questions.explain: Line 11 puts an apostrophe before text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a CR. The name has no comma, quote or line break, so line 12 adds no quotes.

questions.prompt: The search matches 42 invoices and the list shows 25 per page. How many invoice rows does `exportInvoices` return?
options: 42, because the query has no LIMIT
25, the first page only
25 or 17, depending on the `page` parameter
questions.explain: The query on lines 131 to 138 ends with ORDER BY and has no LIMIT or OFFSET. The function also takes no page number.
